title: Apple and rhubarb pots with honey nuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Apples, rhubarb, orange, sugar, butter, nuts, honey and natural yoghurt are all plain kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every item is a routine Tesco buy, and 75g each of almonds and hazelnuts is an everyday cost.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, a frying pan, a knife and bowls, and simmering and toasting are beginner techniques.

works.reason: Three Bramleys and 300g rhubarb stewed in orange juice with 5 tbsp sugar will collapse into a sharp-sweet compote that fills four pots with 400g yoghurt and toasted nuts.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers peeling and chopping the fruit, zesting the orange, chopping and toasting the nuts and layering, and 30 cook minutes fits the simmer plus cooling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon are used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stored Bramleys with early forced rhubarb is a natural April pairing, and the apples are the bulk of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British instructions a neighbour would give.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, yoghurt and nuts make a satisfying snack, and the sugar and honey are moderate when shared across four.
